text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- TRADE WITH THE U.S. MAY BE REVIEWED

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso told Brazil's ambassador to Washington to closely monitor a worrisome $1.6 billion trade gap with the United States. Brasilia is concerned about tariffs imposed on Brazilian orange juice, as well as rises in tariffs on leather, shoes, textiles and other exports.
-- BRAZIL PAID $6.0 BILLION IN INTEREST OVERSEAS

In the first eight months, Brazil paid some $6.00 billion in interest abroad, up 20 percent from the same period last year. Total capital raised overseas reached $48.3 billion in August, up $15 billion from August 1995.
-- BRADESCO ANNOUNCES A DROP IN INTEREST RATES

Largest private Brazilian bank Bradesco yesterday announced a decline in interest rates on personal and business loans. It is the first drop in bank interest rates since June, according to Bradesco executive director Antonio Fernando Burani.
O GLOBO
-- GOVERNMENT CUTS 70,000 JOBS TO SAVE $2.4 BILLION
The Brazilian government will eliminate 70,000 of 140,000 vacant posts and plans to retain the remainder as reserves. The move will save the government some $200 million a month.
-- RADIOBRAS AND CONAB ON PRIVATIZATION LIST
Brazil's federal government has prepared a list of 23 firms that it plans to eliminate, privatize or transfer to states and cities. Under the plan, Radiobras, Conab and other firms would be sold off.
-- NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT BANK MAY FINANCE FIRMS' CASH FLOW
Brazil's National Development Bank, in a bid to help firms raise money in the internal market rather than become indebted overseas, plans a package of measures to promote internal savings.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- SAO PAULO GOVERNOR COVAS WANTS TO DISARM RANCHERS
Sao Paulo state is awaiting a judicial order to begin this week disarming ranchers in the Pontal do Paranapanema region, where disputes with landless peasants threatens to erupt into violence.
-- BANKS IN BRAZIL'S PROER PROGRAM ROLL OVER DEBTS

Six loans from Brazil's Proer program to help troubled banks merge expired in August and were not paid. The loans, totalling 4.918 billion reais and extended by the Central Bank for 90 days, were made to Economico, Banorte and Mercantil banks.
-- INFANT MALNUTRITION FALLS IN BRAZIL
Infant malnutrition in Brazil fell by 16.9 percent between 1989 and 1996, according to a survey by the Health Ministry and UNICEF.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
